Hello everyone, 
I'm new to INLA and have run into what I'm sure must be a problem with my code, what I'm trying to achieve is essentially the same as the Piemonte analysis ( Spatio-temporal modeling of particulate matter concentration through the SPDE approach ) and I've copied the code pretty closely but I get the warning that my "number of unused groups>number of used groups".
I'm sure that this is some kind of misspecification as the error message suggests because I don't get the same warning when I run the Piemonte code. Can anyone give me some insight into the source of the error (I've run through the verbose output and haven't managed to work it out).
Thanks in advance 
Cheers
James

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] number of unused groups>number of used groups
parts:
Thanks for the help! 
It turned out to be a pretty trivial problem I was just calling 3 locations in the loc argument I'm not entirely sure why that was the error that came up but its stopped now and the code is running as expected.

A.est = inla.spde.make.A(mesh,
                         loc=data.matrix(spde_data)[,4:3], #it was data.matrix(spde_data%>%dplyr::select(station, Long,Lat)) which was auto joining the grouping variable 
                           group=data.matrix(spde_data$day),
                         n.group=n_days)
Just put that in in case anyone ever searches and has the same problem. 

Thanks again for your help
Cheers
James
